items.lever: C. better ranking of the documents already in the frozen top-100 pool
items.ceiling_detail: pool-oracle nDCG@10 0.7446 vs frozen 0.3581; perfect ordering of the same 10 returned docs alone is worth 14.55 pts (296/519 queries), so 37.6% of the pool headroom is pure position error

items.lever: A. promote the zero-class documents that are already in the pool

items.lever: D. more replacement swaps at the tail
items.ceiling_detail: 0.37694 (up to 3 tail replacements from union(dense20,CE20)) vs 0.3581; one unlimited swap restricted to ranks 8-10 = 0.40975, any slot = 0.51036
items.evidence: error_analysis_dev.json: 43.6% of single-fix gain sits at ranks 1-3, only 21.4% at 8-10, so a tail-only policy is structurally capped at about a fifth of the replacement headroom; measured capture of the 1.88-pt ceiling is 34.6% (+0.65 pts)

items.lever: B. first-stage recall (deeper or additional retrieval)
items.ceiling_detail: dense@100 pool oracle 0.7446 -> dense@1000 0.9416; 22.5% of dev gold sits between dense rank 100 and 1000; only 10 of the 138 zero queries have no relevant document anywhere in the dense top-1000

items.expected_detail: 0.5% of 19.71 pts (measured probe capture) = +0.10; a hybrid stage that adds only new documents cannot pay unless the CE is retrained on them

largest_ceiling.why: the frozen system already sits on top of a pool whose oracle is 0.7446; the documents are there and half the recoverable nDCG is mis-ordering of the ten docs actually returned. the earlier diagnosis 'the zero class is a first-stage recall failure (130 of 138 unreachable in dense top-100)' is wrong, and its artefact has a parse bug. reteco_server/zero_recall.py reads TREC rows as (docid=p[2], score=float(p[3])) but p[3] is the rank column, so it sorts each run by rank DESCENDING and then keeps the first 100 rows - for a 1000-deep dense run that slice is ranks 901-1000, and inside a 100-deep CE run the reported index is 101-true_rank. Concretely, for bitcoin/112021_76 the gold doc is at dense rank 55 and CE rank 71, yet the artefact records dense best_rank=null and ce best_rank=30 (=101-71). Its frozen column reads runs/sub_sft_e2bc_<d>_dev.trec, which does not exist locally (only the _head10 prefix does), so that column is all null. The correct numbers: gold is inside the dense top-100 for 86 of the 138 zeros (128 inside the top-1000), and 519/519 queries have identical dense-top100 and frozen Rec@100, i.e. the delivered pool holds the same relevant content as the dense top-100. 86 of the zeros are already inside the pool

the earlier 'zeros -> domain non-zero mean = 0.472' is 0.4985 under the stated rule (each zero replaced by its own domain's non-zero mean, 13-domain macro); the domain-median variant asked for here is 0.4385
